scope: Proposition 4.1 (One-step estimates) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ Universality for the Weak Random-Bond Ising Model” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-Universality-for-the-Weak-Random-Bond-Ising-Model-October-5-2026/quenched-sle3-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dbf1578546653fc5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: One can choose L large, then b > 0 small, and finally x∗ > 0 such that for every input field of Section 3 with X ≤ x∗, |m′ − Lm| ≤ CLX2 , Y ′ ≤ ρY + CL(|m| + X2 ), X′ ≤ ρX + CL( √ W + Y ), (4.2) where ρ < 1 and all constants are independent of the scale s. The constants denoted by CL may depend on all the fixed step parameters, including the subsequently chosen b.
